ticket: JSRT-22 (ToPrimitive hint bug: numeric operators used the default hint instead of number)

root_cause.summary: ToNumber/ToNumeric on an object must call ToPrimitive with the "number" hint (7.1.3/7.1.4), not "default". A separate primitive_number_hint() helper already existed and was already used correctly by builtins_binary.rs, builtins_binary_bigint.rs and builtins_date.rs, but the interpreter's own core numeric operators called primitive()/primitive_with_hint(v, false) (default hint) instead.
affected: interp.rs to_number(): the generic ToNumber(object) path (used directly by Math.max/min, to_int32/to_uint32 on an object, array length assignment, etc, and indirectly by every operator below once its own operand primitive is already resolved)
interp_stmt.rs binary() Sub|Mul|Div|Rem|Pow|Shl|Shr|UShr|BitAnd|BitOr|BitXor (13.15.3 ApplyStringOrNumericBinaryOperator's ToNumeric on each operand)
interp_stmt.rs binary() Lt|Gt|Le|Ge (7.2.13 IsLessThan's ToPrimitive(x, number)/ToPrimitive(y, number))
interp_builtins.rs native_number() (Number(value), 21.1.1.1 ToNumeric) -- installed at interp_install.rs but overwritten/dead once builtins_std_number_math.rs runs, fixed anyway for consistency
builtins_std_number_math.rs std_number_constructor() (Number(value), the one actually installed as the global Number)
deliberately_unchanged: binary() BinOp::Add (13.15.3): `+` calls ToPrimitive with no hint (default), since it may end up doing string concatenation instead of numeric addition -- spec-correct as-is.
interp_equality.rs loose_eq() (7.2.14 IsLooselyEqual): object-vs-primitive coercion also has no hint specified (default) -- spec-correct as-is.

builtins_date.rs date_ctor()'s single-argument Date(value) overload (21.4.3.2 `ToPrimitive(value)`, no hint) and date_proto_to_primitive/date_ordinary_to_primitive (Date's own @@toPrimitive, which picks its own order from the passed-in hint argument) -- both already correct, untouched.
interp.rs to_js_string()/to_property_key() (string hint) -- already correct, untouched.
root_cause.observability: Only observable when an operand has a custom @@toPrimitive that inspects its hint argument (e.g. `{[Symbol.toPrimitive](hint){...}}`); ordinary objects relying on valueOf/toString use the identical fallback order for hints "number" and "default" (OrdinaryToPrimitive), so this had zero effect on plain objects/boxed primitives without an exotic @@toPrimitive.

related_bug_found_via_regression_test.summary: Postfix ++/-- returned the raw pre-conversion operand instead of ToNumeric(oldValue) (13.4.2/13.4.3 step "Return oldValue"), invisible for plain numbers (old == ToNumeric(old)) but wrong for objects.
related_bug_found_via_regression_test.fix: interp_stmt.rs update() now converts old to old_numeric via primitive_number_hint() once, passes that (already-primitive) value into update_value() (a no-op re-entry there, not a second ToPrimitive call/side effect), and returns old_numeric for the postfix case instead of the raw old.
related_bug_found_via_regression_test.caught_by: numeric_operators_pass_the_number_hint_to_to_primitive's `o-- === 5` case, added for the hint fix itself; not something the ticket named up front.
related_bug_found_via_regression_test.cross_lane_note: amazing-js/src/vm/mod.rs's Instruction::Update handling (`registers[*dst] = if *prefix { next } else { previous };`) has the identical bug and is js-vm-owned; not touched here. update_value()'s own signature/behavior was left unchanged (still takes a possibly-object JsValue and does the number-hint conversion internally) specifically so vm/mod.rs's existing call site keeps compiling and behaving as before -- filed in questions.md for js-vm to fix or grant a one-line change.

gate.platform: Linux (venus-003, idle dedicated host, load average 0.05-0.19 at measurement time)
gate.before_source: .agents/test262/baseline.json, built at dev 3cbfc982 -- same commit as this ticket's rebase base for crates/amazing-js (git diff 6a002829..3cbfc982 -- crates/amazing-js/src/ is empty, so the source underlying that snapshot is byte-identical there), same timeout_seconds so directly comparable

per_file_diff_vs_baseline.note: All four gains are the postfix ++/-- ToNumeric(oldValue) fix, confirming it against the real corpus, not just the added unit test.
No existing Number() test in this corpus observably distinguishes the number vs default hint.

crate_amazing_js.nextest: 446 tests run: 446 passed, 1 skipped (up from 445 pass/1 skip at JSRT-21's HEAD; +1 is numeric_operators_pass_the_number_hint_to_to_primitive)
crate_amazing_js.note: interp::vm::tests::primitive_and_operator_differential_corpus (tree-walker vs VM parity) still passes -- it does not probe the specific hint-observing-object/postfix-object edge cases this ticket fixed, so it does not (and structurally cannot yet) catch the tree-walker/VM divergence this ticket introduces on those specific cases until js-vm's mirrored bugs are fixed.

known_gaps: amazing-js/src/vm/mod.rs's Instruction::Update handling has the identical postfix-returns-pre-conversion-value bug for object operands; js-vm-owned, filed in questions.md rather than fixed here.

IsLessThan's LeftFirst evaluation-order parameter (7.2.13) is not modeled: binary()'s Lt|Gt|Le|Ge branch always calls primitive_number_hint(a) before primitive_number_hint(b) regardless of operator, but spec evaluates `a > b` as IsLessThan(b, a, false) -- side-effect-observable only when both operands are objects with side-effecting valueOf/toString AND neither has already been resolved to a primitive earlier in evaluation. Noted but not fixed this ticket (scope: hint value, not evaluation order); a candidate for a future, separate, narrow ticket if it surfaces in practice.

primitive_number_hint() and primitive_with_hint() have a pre-existing, unrelated divergence in their internal-slot ([[NumberData]]/[[StringData]]/[[BooleanData]]) fast-path shortcut: primitive_number_hint() only takes the shortcut when the object has neither an own valueOf nor an own toString, while primitive_with_hint() always checks the slots first regardless. Both bypass calling an inherited (possibly monkey-patched) Number.prototype.valueOf/toString for boxed primitives when the shortcut fires, which is not what OrdinaryToPrimitive specifies (it never special-cases internal slots). Observed while reading this code for the hint fix, not exercised by any test262 gain/loss above; flagged as a separate, narrower correctness question, not fixed here to avoid scope creep beyond the named ticket.
